implementation.name: original-v2-pfc-credit-deadlock
implementation.scope: The original four-switch cycle, with four declared toy packet slots per queue. For this toy only, full queues pause their predecessor and any free slot allows resume. A watchdog drops one packet; real thresholds and recovery policies vary.
implementation.question: What must change before a deadlocked queue can forward?

purpose: What must change before a deadlocked queue can forward?
storyboard: Each queue holds four packets. Its head packet needs a slot in the next queue clockwise, but no next queue has space.
Each full queue sends PAUSE counterclockwise to its predecessor. Packet forwarding dependencies still point clockwise.
No packet can advance: every head waits for a full downstream queue, and every sender is paused. Waiting alone cannot make space.
An external watchdog drops A0 from queue 1. This is packet loss, not successful delivery. The new free slot allows queue 4 to resume in this declared toy.
D0 advances clockwise from queue 4 into the free slot in queue 1. Queue 4 now has the free slot.
C0 advances clockwise into queue 4. The free slot moves upstream to queue 3.
B0 advances clockwise into queue 3. Queue 2 can now accept a packet.
A1 advances clockwise into queue 2. The cycle has made progress because recovery created space; the discarded A0 still requires transport recovery.
guard: PAUSE direction is opposite to the packet dependency. No queue drains while all are full. Watchdog drop is recorded as loss; resumption is conditional on the explicitly simplified threshold rule.
